sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r6/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 34 (#33 criterion_description_is_self_consistent) and Internal Quality Checks row 34 annotation (Mukesh: multiple verifiers combined in one flow)
.qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r6/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/SKILL.md (Known false positives: one criterion covering a whole flow, checks 26/28/33)
evidence: Reviewed all 26 criteria (2 gates, 16 functional, 6 polish, 4 visual). No criterion enumerates requirements and then waives most of them. Functional criteria are conjunctive bars with numbered legs and a 'Fails if' summary; functional/prompt.md:32-33 resolves any summary/leg divergence explicitly: 'A criterion passes only if every numbered leg and every listed positive control holds; its "Fails if" line names the main failures but never excuses a leg it does not mention.' Part A/B criteria end with 'Both parts must hold' (e.g. functional/judge.toml:51,82,128,179,231; 'All three parts' :263). Tolerances such as timer_changes leg 2 ('a not-available answer, an error or an empty list are all fine, as long as neither "2,400" nor "4,200" appears', judge.toml:139) define one acceptable outcome set, not a waiver. Gate scope sentences (render:32 'basic reachability/sign-in gate only. Assign 1 only if every check holds'; constraints:35-36 'does not grade roles, correctness, or feature completeness') exclude unlisted topics without waiving listed steps. visual matter_sidebar (visual/judge.toml:8) conditionally drops one of three anchor facets ('If no matter shows an unread count when you look, judge identification and selection only') - an observable, state-dependent condition needed because polish/functional runs may leave Gwen with no unread matters (seed read_up_to plus later reads), and unread counts are graded functionally (unread_and_new_messages_line); this is one bar per observed state, not two targets. Note-level residual: the polish prompt lacks the functional prompt's 'Fails if never excuses a leg' rule, and three polish 'Fails if' lines omit a body leg: enter_sends (polish/judge.toml:7, 'message box is empty afterwards' not in Fails-if), link_highlight (:34, 'still highlighted about ten seconds later' - a public requirement, conversations.md:17 'stays highlighted until you open something else' - only implicitly covered by 'nothing sets it apart'), refusal_in_place (:52, 'sign in with the right password: no reason is shown'). These are non-exclusive summaries, not waivers, so they do not meet the row's defect definition, but a judge reading Fails-if as exhaustive could pass e.g. a 2-second flash highlight or a box that keeps sent text. No runtime judge evidence was needed or used for this textual row.
counterexample: Not a blocking counterexample: a polish judge that treats 'Fails if' as exhaustive could pass link_highlight for a highlight that fades after ~2s (body requires it still highlighted at ~10s) or enter_sends for an app that sends once but leaves the text in the box.
suggested_fix: Optional: add the functional prompt's sentence ('every numbered leg/sentence must hold; the Fails if line never excuses a step it does not mention') to scored/polish/prompt.md, or add the omitted legs to those three Fails-if lines.
